correctness.rationale: Definition 4.10 confirmed from the original PDF. Top and meet laws classify Box via z=Box 0; Dunn gives Box <= Diamond, z<=t, and the remaining cross-atom restrictions. Disjoint cases z=1, z=atom, z=0 with t=1/atom/0 yield exact algebraic summands in RESULT.md. Formula holds by bijective case count for every n>=3. The packaged stdlib Python implementation tests every defining axiom directly for n=3 and n=4, compares 574 and 5054 with formula, and independently checks Burnside counts 126 and 325 via all automorphisms. Computation only supports finite cases, not all-width induction; the combinatorial proof supplies the universal quantifier.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the width-uniform exact count and case normal form for all non-distributive M_n with Definition 4.10 modalities, plus complete n=3,4 orbit counts. The primary article gives the axioms and duality, not the specific formula; an earlier thesis has stronger, different diamond axioms; positive modal algebra research restricted to distributive lattices cannot imply it. Completed semantic, synonym, numeric, and title/author searches against published findings and published primary sources returned no statement or stronger enumeration covering this claim. Prior published work on finite Gödel chains and frames concerns non-isomorphic carrier structures and non-equivalent axioms. Unindexed alternative presentations and indirect deductions remain residual risks.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently termed enumeration of this exact class could exist; semantic search and inspected literature cannot certify uniqueness.
General duality may enable another author to derive these counts as an unreported corollary; the exact formula is not explicit in the relevant inspected works.
The original 2021 thesis studies a stricter and not fully identical operator class; uninspected alternate presentations may blur this comparison.

value.rationale: M_n is the natural height-two atom lattice, with n=3 its first non-distributive example, directly motivated by extending positive modal logic beyond distributivity. Complete classification of all two-operator modal expansions for arbitrary n provides a genuinely variable-width exact enumerator, identifies five structural regimes driven by bottom images and Dunn restrictions, and settles minimal non-distributive isomorphism counts. It is not a trivial specialization of distributive positive modal algebra counts or a tabulation of a fixed arbitrary model; n=3 is the natural minimal case and n=4 the next case. The calculation distinguishes the later minimal monotonic diamond axioms from the earlier stricter join- and bottom-preserving formulation. Future frame/model theory can use exact finite test-family sizes; this is potential use, not an asserted downstream theorem.
